Victor Mikhailovich Vasnetsov - The Sleeping Princess

There's a lot going on in this painting. Sleeping beauty seems to have been pricked by a magic spindle -- you can see it on the floor, beside one of her slippers, which has fallen off. She looks about to fall off her couch herself, but her crown remains firmly around her head. Everyone is asleep, even the birds and the beasts. We've got a bear, a fox and a hare around her bed. Peacocks roost in the trees and swans sleep on the pond. They've all been asleep a long time -- notice the grass and weeds growing up through the cracks in the floorboards. The palace beyond appears deserted. I wonder what the big book open before the couch of the princess signifies? It almost looks like the princess is missing the end of the baby finger from her left hand, but maybe that's just the angle of the finger. The faces of a man and a woman gaze down solemnly from the tops of the two pillars behind the princess. They are probably intended to represent the loving union of marriage. Or they may be spiritual guardians.
